questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem:
Vihaan is preparing a project on how candidates are chosen for a general election, and finds that the USA and India follow different methods. Consider the following statements.
1. In the USA the members and supporters of a party choose its candidates, whereas in India the top party leaders of the party choose the candidates who will contest the election.
2. This difference exists because in the USA political parties are not permitted to contest elections, so their members and supporters have to pick the candidates on their own.
Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem:
In her classroom, Sara and her friends keep arguing about the steps a government should take on school fees, water supply and the cost of textbooks, and they agree that a government cannot act on every opinion that people hold. Consider the following statements.
1. Political parties put forward different policies and programmes, and the voters choose from them.
2. This is how a large number of similar opinions get grouped together to provide a direction in which policies can be formulated by the governments, since no government can handle such a large variety of views.
Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.stem:
Kabir's class is asked to imagine a general election held without any political parties, where every candidate stands on his own. Consider the following statements.
1. In such an election every candidate would be independent, so no one would be able to make any promises to the people about any major policies.
2. This would happen because political parties play a decisive role in making laws for a country.
Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
